ORDER These Miscellaneous Appeals under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act have been filed against the award dated 01.10.2019 passed by Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Satna in MACC No.100333/2016.

entities.text: Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Satna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.A. No.2379/2020 has been filed by the claimants for enhancement of compensation amount whereas M.A. No.1970/2020 has been filed by Insurance Company.
Accordingly, by this common order, both the miscellaneous appeals shall be decided.

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed mainly on the ground that the vehicle in question was implanted and there is a violation of insurance policy because the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence.

3. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal in short are that on 09.09.2015, after performing the duties, the husband of claimant No.1 Late Shri Basantlal Prajapati was coming back to his house on his motorcycle.

At about 7.35 pm, when he reached in front of High School Takhatpur, it is alleged that the driver of the truck bearing registration No.C.G.10A-1035 by driving the truck in rash and negligent manner, dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased suffered grievous injuries and succumbed to the same.

The age of the deceased was 48 years and he was posted as Head Constable in Chhattisgarh Police and his monthly income was Rs.35,000/-.
4.
It is the case of the claimants that after the accident they are residing within the territorial jurisdiction of MACT Satna.
The non- applicants No.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner of the truck remained ex- parte and accordingly, they were proceeded ex-parte.

The appellant filed its written statement and claimed that in fact the deceased himself was driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and met with an accident as he himself lost his control over the motorcycle.
The truck has been wrongly implanted and the claim petition has been filed on false averments.
The driver of the offending truck was not having valid driving licence and the truck was being plied without any valid permit and fitness.

5. The appellant has examined Vedram Sahu (D.W.1), who has stated that he was posted as Data Entry Operator in License Branch, R.T.O., Bilaspur and the driver of the offending vehicle was having a driving licence to drive L.M.V.

Thus, it is submitted that since the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a driving licence to drive L.M.V., therefore, he was not eligible to drive Smt. Kailashwati vs Yogesh Sahu on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142862486/
5
commercial
vehicle.
6. The submissions made by the counsel for the appellant is no more res intigra.

7. The Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663 has held as under :
60.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
60.1.
"Light motor vehicle" as defined in Section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in Section 2(21) read with Sections 2(15) and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act 54 of 1994. 60.2.

A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a roadroller, "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under Section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54 of 1994 and 28-3-2001 in the form.

60.3. The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act 54 of 1994 w.e.f. 14-11-1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of Section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(e), "medium passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(f), "heavy goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(h) with expression "transport vehicle" as substituted in Section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of Section 10(2)(d) and Section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle. 60.4.

The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle"
is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle"
continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.

8. So far as the false involvement of the truck in question is concerned, the counsel for the appellant by referring to the FIR (Exhibit P/2) submitted that in the FIR it was mentioned that some unknown big vehicle has committed an offence and therefore, it is claimed that the truck in question was falsely implanted at a later stage.

6 9.
Considered the submissions made by the counsel for the appellant.
10. The claimants have examined Pal Singh (P.W.3).
This witness has specifically stated that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle.
This witness in his cross-examination specifically denied that the offending vehicle after causing the accident had overtaken the car of this witness.
This witness also denied that after the accident they stopped on the spot and also took the injured to the hospital.
On his own, this witness clarified that since relative had to catch train, therefore, they directly went to Bilaspur Railway Station.
He further claimed that they had chased the offending vehicle and had noted down its registration number.
He denied that the driver of the motorcycle was driving the motorcycle in mid of the road.
11. It is true that in the FIR registration number of the vehicle was not disclosed but the FIR, Exhibit P/2, was not lodged by an eye witness.
Complainant Dalveer Prajapati had specifically mentioned in the FIR that he received the information regarding accident on phone.
The counsel for the appellant could not point out any good reason to disbelieve the evidence of Pal Singh (P.W.3).
It is well known that generally, the independent witnesses do not voluntarily come forward for various reasons.

Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the offence was committed by the offending truck bearing registration No.C.G.10A-1035.
12.
The appellants have valued the appeal at Rs.1,00,000/- and has paid the Court fee of Rs.2,500/-.
13. A solitary contention has been raised by the counsel for the appellants that the deceased was survived by his widow and four children.
However, the Claims Tribunal has awarded consortium only to the wife.

14. Accordingly, it is held that all the four children are entitled for consortium @
Rs.40,000/-, therefore, the compensation is liable to be enhanced by a further amount of Rs.1,60,000/-.
15. Since the appeal has been valued at Rs.1,00,000/-, therefore, the compensation amount is enhanced by a further amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Other conditions of the award shall remain the same.
16. With aforesaid modification, the award dated 01.10.2019 passed by Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Satna in MACC No.100333/2016 is hereby affirmed.

Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the offence was committed by the offending truck bearing registration No.C.G.10A-1035.
12.
